title: es-ES object bundle carries `rol`→`puesto` find-replace damage (`Puestoes`, `contpuesto`, a surviving `Clonar rol`)
body:
Tripped over while implementing #8601 (which corrects a *different* class of defect in these same files — an inaccurate uniqueness claim). This card is about **shipped Spanish that is simply broken**, not about a claim that disagrees with the source.

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts` reads as though a global `rol` to `puesto` find-replace was run over it at some point, without review of the results.

## Instances observed

| line | shipped today | problem |
|---|---|---|
| `:13` | `pluralLabel: "Puestoes"` | not a Spanish word; the plural of `puesto` is `Puestos` |
| `:15` | `description: "Definiciones de puesto para el contpuesto de acceso RBAC"` | `control` was itself caught by the replace and mangled into `contpuesto`. Should read `control de acceso`. |
| `:91` | `clone_position.label: "Clonar rol"` | the replace *missed* this one, so it still says `rol` while the rest of the object says `puesto` |

`:15` is the clearest tell: `con` + `trol` became `con` + `tpuesto`, which only happens if the replace was substring-based and unreviewed. `:91` is the same event's other half — one instance it should have changed and did not.

These are all `sys_position`. An admin using Setup in Spanish sees `Puestoes` as the object's plural label in navigation and list views.

## ⚠️ This is a SAMPLE, not a bounded set

I did **not** sweep for further instances. #8601 explicitly forbade the bundle sweep (`"do not do the sweep for other stale bundles the card suggests — that is a separate card if wanted, not a rider on this one"`), so I recorded only what I saw while reading the exact lines that card needed. The same find-replace would plausibly have touched other objects in this bundle, and possibly other `es-ES` bundles in other packages. **Anyone picking this up should begin by bounding it**, not by fixing these three lines.

## Not caught by any gate

Same blind spot as #8601: `check:i18n` compares bundle *structure* against what the extractor emits and is green either way, so nothing mechanical judges whether a translated string is good Spanish. See #8543 for why merge mode leaves existing values untouched.

## Fix shape

Leaf string values only, per the bundle header's documented workflow — the same route #8601 used. No generator change.

## Related

- #8601 — the uniqueness-claim defect in these same files; different class, fixed separately in PR #8723.
- #8543 — the generator defect that leaves existing leaf values untouched, so drift and damage both survive silently.
